note: PLAT-012 declare SDK perimeter: a release that needs a proprietary SDK is allowed, but the boundary has to be stated. src/platform/perimeter.zig makes three things explicit - which component is the SDK, its redistribution policy per component (redistributable, proprietary, restricted, or unclassified), and which side of the build/runtime boundary it lands on - and refuses a plan that leaves any of them unstated. The failure shapes are distinguished on purpose: an unclassified licence is refused wherever it sits, because publishing what nobody has classified is not a decision to make by omission; a proprietary or restricted component in the *payload* is a separate refusal, which is the SDK-shipped-by-accident mistake the case exists to prevent; and a plan that requires an SDK without naming one is refused, because an unnamed boundary is not a boundary. The report returns the shipped set, the build-only set, and the SDK by name, so the boundary is auditable rather than implied. Fault proof: allowing a non-redistributable component into the payload makes the leak assertions fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
